summary: Sacks views PayPal as a legacy product growing only 7% annually with an outdated interaction model, attracting acquisition interest primarily because its market cap is deeply beaten down from a $322B peak to ~$30-40B, and believes it needs a visionary operator to resuscitate it.
quote: the product is getting very long in the tooth. I think it's only growing 7% a year... the product has become somewhat obsolete, and in a way it's a legacy product... The reason why it's attracting offers is it's so beaten up.

quote: The price is probably another 10 to 15% higher from here. And, and I will say that there is a certain individual that must look very closely at putting in a competitive bid.
